messages:
ara: FYI rolling canary for kernel-router v3 -> observed a few OOMs on longctx nightly job, looks like memory climbed steadily before OOMs :thinking:
sam: ugh, saw CI perf failures too. matrix-batcher tests spiked tail latency 3x. could be related to the batching heuristics change in #4107
maria: what error logs do we have? paste from one of the failed hosts
ara: paste logs from host:
```
[2026-03-17T23:12:14Z] runtime: oom while allocating 2147483648 bytes
[2026-03-17T23:12:14Z] kv-cache: slab allocation failed: no contiguous region
[2026-03-17T23:12:14Z] kernel-router: fallback to generic kernel; large-alloc path increased
```
sam: interesting—kv slab allocator complaining about fragmentation. I also see long-lived KV entries not being compacted by the new eviction path
perf-bot: perf anomaly detected: kv-frag-index increased by 28% after merge ab12c3d (#4107); end-to-end token throughput down 12%
kevin: I ran a heap profile on the canary host, attaching snippet (trimmed):
```
malloc: heap growth at kv-slab: 1.9GB
hot objects: kv-entry(64B) * 18M, kv-metadata * 2.1M
fragmentation estimate: 22%
```
maria: does the PR touch kernel selection or batcher timeouts? I thought it was meant to be a small batching heuristic tweak
sam: it was a batching heuristic + micro change to kernel selection fallback ordering to prefer vectorized kernels when seq_len > 512. The heuristic also pushes borderline ops into large-batch path which holds KV cache slots longer
ara: repro locally with the longctx job + synthetic workload: enable new batcher + kernel-router -> replication of memory drift in ~10 minutes
kevin: ran bisect: suspect commit is ab12c3d -> the change in fallback ordering + batch hold tweak
maria: can we do a quick canary revert to confirm? if revert fixes, put rollout on hold
ara: did a canary revert of #4107 on one pool at 23:45. memory growth stopped on that pool within two minutes, canary with patch still growing
ops-bot: Rollout paused for kernel-router v3 (canary) by ara at 2026-03-17T23:50:02Z
sam: OK that suggests causality. next steps: 1) open perf bisect issue (assign to eng-runtime), 2) capture full heap dumps, 3) instrument KV slab to emit free/used histogram per slab-size
maria: I'm adding improved unit tests for eviction: ensure older small entries get compacted when large-batch hold > X ms
kevin: quick hack: lowered batch hold timeout back to previous value and re-ran local longctx job -> memory stabilized. So batching hold seems like the accelerant for fragmentation
ara: filing rollback PR now and flagging as rollout-blocker. also add a watch on kv-frag-index and longctx mem slope
sam: thanks. after rollback we'll prepare a focused change that separates kernel selection policy from batch hold behavior so we can land the safe part
maria: noted. will add regression test and a perf gate in CI for kv-frag-index delta > 10%
perf-bot: created perf-issue #5478 (link: https://redwood.example/issue/5478) summarizing findings and bisect log
kevin: saved heap profiles to s3://redwood-perf/2187654321/ and uploaded the pmap dumps in the ticket
ara: thumbs up. keeping rollout on hold until we have a patch + tests. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
